title: Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) System Reference: Member Election of Wholesale-Supplier Pass-Through Rows for Early Retirement
content:
# Member Election of Pass-Through Rows for Early Retirement

*Member information system reference — Capital Credits (Patronage Capital).*

## Rule for the election

A wholesale-supplier pass-through allocation of a former member's account is retired early under an approved discounted early retirement request only on the member's own election, one election entry for each pass-through allocation year the member chooses, and a pass-through allocation the member does not elect stays in the general rotation.

Each elected row is booked as one special retirement entry with retirement type discounted early for its gross, together with one payable entry for the payable the member accepts, and the gross is the pass-through amount of that allocation year less every general retirement already booked on it.

## Booking an elected row

A pass-through row elected under an approved discounted early retirement has its payable fixed only after the account carries the payable entry for the distribution-margin allocation that the request covers.

Put the other way: while the account does not yet carry that payable entry for the distribution-margin allocation the approved request covers, the payable of an elected pass-through row is not yet fixed.

## What the election records

One election, for one pass-through allocation year:

- records a special retirement entry of the discounted early type, source wholesale-supplier pass-through, for the gross allocated amount;
- records the matching payable entry for the amount the member accepts, net of the discount;
- lowers the account's unretired credits by the gross and raises its retired credits owed by the payable.

The member sees the accepted amount owed on the account. A year the member does not elect is left unretired and stays in the general rotation.

## Invoking the tool

The tool is `elect_passthrough_early_retirement_2ee4171d`, a member-owned tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves — the former member — runs it with `call_user_discoverable_tool`. The election is the member's own act.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `capital_account_id` | reference number of the member's capital credit account, from the capital credit account lookup, as the agent reads it to the member | identifier |
| `capital_request_id` | reference number of the member's approved discounted early retirement request, from the capital credit request lookup, as the agent reads it to the member | identifier |
| `allocation_year` | the patronage year of the pass-through allocation elected, as on the allocation entry | four digits, YYYY |
| `gross_retired_amount` | the allocated pass-through amount of that year being retired | USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent |
| `payable_amount` | the discounted amount the member accepts for that row | USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent |

The source of the row is always recorded as `gt_allocation` and the retirement type as `discounted_early`; neither is a parameter.

### Return

A successful call returns `status` "elected", `retirement_entry_id`, `payable_entry_id`, `allocation_year` (YYYY), `allocation_source` (always `gt_allocation`), `gross_retired_amount`, `discount_amount` and `payable_amount` (USD, 2 decimals), and the account's new `unretired_balance` and `payable_balance` (USD, 2 decimals). The election succeeded when the status is elected.
